exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: Pregnant mothers who delivered in university hospitals of Ahvaz, southwest of Iran between 2020 and 2022 and were subsequently readmitted during their postpartum period.
finding: The overall prevalence of postpartum readmission was 1.39%, with febrile complications, particularly metritis and pelvic abscess, being the most common causes.
mod_finding: Patients undergoing Cesarean Section (CS) had greater rates of postpartum readmission, morbidity, longer length of hospital stay, and higher incidences of pelvic abscess and blood transfusion compared to those with vaginal deliveries.
